candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — infection surveillance, outbreak response and transmission prevention
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize core steps in investigating and controlling a healthcare-associated infection outbreak.

options.A: Assume the cluster is coincidental unless every case has an identical organism.
options.B: Delay data collection and control measures until additional infections occur.
options.C: Close the entire hospital before defining cases or assessing transmission.
options.D: Establish a case definition, identify and characterize cases, evaluate likely exposures or transmission routes, and implement targeted control measures.

candidate.rationale: CDC's healthcare-setting field investigation process includes establishing case definitions, identifying and counting cases, organizing and analyzing data, forming and testing hypotheses, performing infection-control assessment, and implementing control measures. Therefore D is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Healthcare outbreak investigation uses a stepwise process including case definition, case finding, exposure/data analysis, hypothesis testing, infection-control assessment, and targeted control measures.
candidate.source_locator: Field Investigation — Steps 4-9: Establish case definitions; Identify and count cases; Organize data; Formulate/test hypotheses; Infection control assessment and implementation of control measures
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
candidate.stem: An infection-prevention team is investigating a cluster of healthcare-associated infections on one unit. Which action is part of the standard outbreak-investigation process?
